claim_being_audited: That the model can be certified for launch on a limited basis because aggregate readiness passed, rehearsal had no severity-one incidents, rollout starts at 3% with rollback and monitoring, and the exposed health-plan benefits support weakness can be handled through launch-time model-card disclosure rather than exclusion or approved risk acceptance.
decision_criteria: If the affected health-plan benefits support use case remains exposed, policy requires disclosure duties to be satisfied at launch; rollout controls alone are insufficient.
If the use case is not excluded and there is no approved risk acceptance, certification support must rest on evidenced launch-time disclosure, not on planned disclosure alone.
Aggregate readiness, no severity-one rehearsal incidents, rollback, and monitoring are supportive context but not substitutes for the policy predicate tied to the exposed segment.
evidence_requests: Provide the launch-time model card or exact disclosure text covering the health-plan benefits support limitation for the exposed initial cohort.
Provide admissible evidence that the disclosed limitation was reviewed and approved for launch.
Provide evidence showing whether the affected use case is in fact excluded from the initial cohort, if that has changed.
Provide any finalized reviewed risk-acceptance record if the organization intends to rely on acceptance instead of exclusion.
specific_concerns: The policy expressly says rollout controls and monitoring do not remove disclosure duties when the affected segment remains exposed.
The actor summary says the health-plan benefits support segment remains below target and is not excluded from the initial cohort.
The available risk-acceptance draft is described as incomplete and not approved on its face.
No admissible evidence is provided showing the actual launch-time model card contains the required limitation disclosure for the exposed use case.
The certification recommendation depends on a disclosure step that is asserted in summary form rather than evidenced directly.
unsupported_claims: That certification is presently supportable, rather than only conditionally supportable, without the actual launch-time disclosure artifact or equivalent admissible proof.
That public guidance on monitoring and model cards is sufficient to bridge the policy requirement for an exposed affected use case.
Any implication that aggregate readiness and staged rollout materially cure the model-card weakness by themselves.
